description: We’re a team of 3 building TrendTrial for the Earth System Trend Detective challenge: a tool that tells you whether a trend in NASA data is robust, fragile, or an instrument artifact. We bring Python, data science, statistics and ML skills. We’d love to add: a geospatial/remote-sensing person (xarray, GIS), a climate science enthusiast, or a UI/storytelling designer. Join us if you like rigorous science and clear, honest storytelling!
summary: Earth System Trend Detective is an open-source scientific platform designed to detect, quantify, and explain long-term climate and environmental shifts using authentic Earth observation records. We developed an automated, end-to-end data pipeline that seamlessly bridges interactive user polygon selections with NASA’s Common Metadata Repository (CMR), AppEEARS, and NOAA archives. The system ingests multidimensional satellite granules (such as GPM IMERG precipitation and MODIS vegetation data), performs area-weighted spatial extraction, and executes rigorous non-parametric statistical tests—including the Seasonal Mann-Kendall test and Sen’s Slope Estimator—to decouple cyclical monsoon variations from true decadal trends. By automating multi-gigabyte data handling in an intuitive browser interface with a 3D WebGL Earth visualization, the platform eliminates dependencies on expensive, specialized GIS software. Built with Python, FastAPI, and React, Earth System Trend Detective delivers peer-reviewed, reproducible climate intelligence directly into the hands of farmers, urban planners, educators, and researchers—transforming complex satellite archives into an actionable public asset for global resilience.
details:
Earth System Trend Detective is an open-source scientific platform designed to detect, quantify, and explain long-term climate and environmental shifts across the globe using authentic Earth observation records. It solves the accessibility gap in climate intelligence by replacing dependency on complex, expensive desktop GIS software with an automated, browser-based pipeline that bridges raw NASA and NOAA satellite archives with peer-reviewed statistical trend analytics.

How It Works:

A user interactively draws any geographic boundary (Polygon) on a map and selects an environmental variable (such as precipitation, vegetation health, or surface temperature) alongside a 20-year timeframe (e.g., 2005–2025). The platform's internal registry routes the query to dedicated acquisition pipelines that interface directly with NASA's Common Metadata Repository (CMR) via earthaccess and AppEEARS APIs. Real multidimensional satellite granules (e.g., GPM IMERG HDF5 files) are downloaded, validated for file integrity, and normalized through xarray and pandas. The engine then performs area-weighted polygon clipping and executes the Seasonal Mann-Kendall test and Sen’s Slope Estimator to filter out recurring seasonal monsoon peaks and determine the true decadal rate of change in physical units per year, returning both visual time series and reproducible academic reports.

Benefits:

Universal Accessibility: Automates multi-gigabyte satellite extraction and coordinate transformation directly in a web browser without requiring GIS software like ArcGIS or QGIS.

100% Scientific Rigor: Operates exclusively on genuine NASA and NOAA observations with zero simulated data or placeholder statistics.

Seasonality Decoupling: Separates cyclical natural variations (such as annual monsoon cycles) from genuine long-term wetting or drying trends.

Hyper-Local Customization: Allows researchers to isolate specific river basins, agricultural districts, or coastal belts rather than relying on generalized national averages.

Complete Reproducibility: Generates downloadable reports (CSV, JSON, PDF) complete with dataset versions, source URLs, missing data percentages, and statistical formulas for academic peer review.

Intended Impact:

Earth System Trend Detective empowers farmers, urban planners, educators, and climate researchers with verifiable, empirical satellite intelligence. It strengthens agricultural adaptation by confirming whether water shortages are temporary seasonal dips or persistent multi-decadal declines. Municipalities can plan flood resilience and urban heat mitigation based on 20-year trends, while universities and grassroots organizations worldwide gain democratic, cluster-free access to NASA's public earth observation data.

Development Tools and Technology Stack:

Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet / React-Leaflet (for interactive polygon selection), and Chart.js (for time-series and trend visualization).

Showcase & 3D Visualization: Lightweight WebGL interface powered by Three.js featuring an interactive 3D Earth globe with procedural atmospheric shaders, cloud rotation, and day/night textures.

Backend & API: Python 3.11, FastAPI (asynchronous REST API), Pydantic v2 (validation schemas), SQLAlchemy, and SQLite (persistent investigation tracking).

Scientific & Spatial Computing: xarray, pandas, numpy, geopandas, shapely (for spatial masking and area-weighted aggregation), and pymannkendall (for non-parametric trend statistics).

Data Ingestion & APIs: earthaccess, NASA Common Metadata Repository (CMR) API, NASA AppEEARS REST API, and NOAA Climate Data Online (CDO) API.

AI & Development Acceleration: Claude Code used as an agentic software engineering assistant to architect pipelines, enforce type safety, implement mathematical algorithms, and optimize frontend-backend integration.

Deployment: Docker, GitHub (indhiran08-coder/EARTH-SYSTEM-TREND-DETECTIVE), and Vercel.

Creativity and Innovation:

The project reimagines satellite climate analysis as an open, accessible public intelligence tool rather than a siloed academic workflow. Its registry-first abstraction decouples human-understandable questions from cryptic mission codes—users simply select "Precipitation" without needing to parse product identifiers like GPM_3IMERGM V07. In addition to aggregated regional figures, the platform can compute Sen’s slope at individual grid cells, producing a localized spatial heatmap that shows micro-climate divergence (e.g., coastal wetting while inland areas experience drought within the same region). On the presentation side, the platform pairs an analytical tool with a cinematic 3D WebGL showcase that makes complex planetary data visually captivating and intuitive for non-technical audiences.

Design Considerations:

Scientific Integrity: Zero tolerance for fabricated data; if a provider is unreachable, the engine transparently logs the limitation instead of returning synthetic results.

Seasonality & Autocorrelation: Specifically accounts for serial correlation and seasonal cycles in climate data to prevent false-positive trend detection.

Web Performance: Heavy satellite granules are clipped and processed asynchronously server-side, transferring only lightweight, ready-to-render JSON to the user's browser.

Unit Provenance: Enforces strict physical unit standardization (e.g., converting precipitation rates into mm/month per year) to ensure scientific accuracy across multi-sensor datasets.

Open Science Compliance: Built completely with open-source dependencies under the MIT license, adhering strictly to NASA’s open-data mandates for global usability.

In essence, Earth System Trend Detective is more than just a climate dashboard—it is an automated bridge between NASA's spaceborne sensors and on-the-ground decision-makers, turning decades of Earth observation into clear, actionable, and mathematically proven climate intelligence for communities worldwide.
